subject: Fail to pass "make test-all" in 32bit/64bit environment in Windows 7.

messages.author: 7d6a5c272d24acfa
messages.subject: Fail to pass "make test-all" in 32bit/64bit environment in Windows 7.
parts:
Hi,

   I have tried to compile STAN(2.1.0 release version) in Windows 7 64bit using Rtools 3.0 as recommended in the manual. My initial intent was to use STAN in visual studio, but at least I wanted to make sure I can compile STAN and pass all tests (which was failed, tho).

Unfortunately, when I attempted to test the compiled library using make build and make test-all, the test failed at test\agrad\fwd\matrix\mdivide_right_tri_low_test.cpp. Also, I attempted 32bit build in the different folder(with clean source files) using make BIT=32 build and make BIT=32 test-all, but it resulted in the same result.

Out of 56 tests, 8 tests failed which are:
AgradFwdMatrixMdivideLeftTriLow.fv_vector_fv_matrix_fv_2ndDeriv
AgradFwdMatrixMdivideLeftTriLow.fv_vector_matrix_fv_2ndDeriv
AgradFwdMatrixMdivideLeftTriLow.fv_matrix_fv_matrix_fv_2ndDeriv
AgradFwdMatrixMdivideLeftTriLow.fv_matrix_fv_matrix_1stDeriv
AgradFwdMatrixMdivideLeftTriLow.ffv_vector_ffv_matrix_ffv_2ndDeriv_2
AgradFwdMatrixMdivideLeftTriLow.ffv_vector_matrix_ffv_2ndDeriv_2
AgradFwdMatrixMdivideLeftTriLow.ffv_matrix_matrix_ffv_2ndDeriv_2
AgradFwdMatrixMdivideLeftTriLow.ffv_matrix_ffv_matrix_1stDeriv

It seems like errors related with Eigen library. I am not sure it is safe to ignore these errors. Any ideas?

Thank you for your attention and help.

Shota

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fail to pass "make test-all" in 32bit/64bit environment in Windows 7.
parts:
Hi Shota,

I've been able to compile Stan on a Windows 7 64bit machine with Rtools 3.0, but we haven't tried with Visual Studio.

Let's try to get you set up with the 64 bit build first.

What are you typing (exactly) and what's the error? You should be able to type:
    make test-all -j4
and it should work. The "-j" flag is to parallelize the build.

Can you double check the g++ version? And can you also make sure the working directory is clean? You can't mix the built libraries between the 32 bit build and the 64 bit build.


Daniel

Hi Daniel,

   Sorry for confusion. I used g++ for this test purpose. I just wanted to make sure everything functional before moving into visual studio.

The version of g++ was 4.6.3, which should come with rtools 3.0 (the manual said the latest frozen version, so I used 3.0).

For 32bit build, I used (in a separate folder from 64bit. I modified the makefile(os_win, line 20) to set 32 bit)

make clean-all
make build
make test-all

and I confirmed I got the same errors.

Let me recompile 64 bit test again. I think I misread 32bit errors as 64bit errors... :(

Thank you for your help.

Shota
